features.feature_value: Chose keep/remove based on whether posts were respectful and fact-based, not which political side they represented; having both versions helped check consistency.
features.evidence_span: focused on whether each post was respectful and fact-based, rather than which side it took
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states their criteria centered on respect/factualness rather than stance, and that the pair helped them judge similarly across political versions.

features.feature_value: Removed posts containing personal attacks or obvious vulgar language.
features.evidence_span: If there were personal attacks between posters I would remove them. If there is obvious vulgar language I would remove them.
features.rationale: Their reflection names specific disqualifying content types that trigger removal.

features.feature_value: Removed inflammatory content when it was intended only to be inflammatory rather than to support civil discussion.
features.evidence_span: inflammatory just to be inflammatory were removed
features.rationale: They tie removal to whether inflammatory statements serve substantive civil discussion versus being performatively inflammatory.

features.feature_value: Flagged excessive profanity or hate speech as grounds for removal.
features.rationale: The participant directly labels profanity/hate as the relevant cue impacting decisions.

features.feature_value: Evaluated curse words and viewed them as unnecessary, implying they reduce keep likelihood.
features.evidence_span: I also evaluated the curse words. I think those were unnecessary.
features.rationale: They indicate they considered profanity (curse words) and judged it unwarranted, linking it to their decision process.

features.feature_value: Removed posts with offensive language and potential threats; otherwise kept posts representing differing opinions.
features.evidence_span: removed the posts with offensive language and what could be seen as a threat
features.rationale: They specify both removal triggers (offensive language, threats) and the default to keep for non-offensive differing opinions.

features.feature_value: Allowed both to pass when they were just opinions without expletives.
features.evidence_span: If they were just opinions expressed without expletive then I let both pass.
features.rationale: They describe a conditional rule: keep if content is opinion only and lacks expletives.

features.feature_value: Was influenced because both messages were constructive and enabled discussion/debate.
features.evidence_span: both messages were constructive in the sense that they allowed for an actual discussion or debate to be had
features.rationale: They state the influence came from constructive/dialectical value, indicating a positive evaluative basis for keep decisions.
